title: Mitigating Backdoors in Masked Diffusion Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.28640v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Masked diffusion language models (MDLMs) have emerged as a promising alternative to autoregressive models because they can predict multiple tokens in parallel rather than generating tokens sequentially. However, recent studies have shown that MDLMs are vulnerable to backdoor attacks: when an input contains an attacker-chosen trigger, a backdoored model generates a targeted output, such as malicious code, while otherwise behaving normally. Despite this threat, backdoor defenses for MDLMs remain largely underexplored. We present UNMASK, the first defense framework for MDLMs that detects trigger-containing inputs, localizes the trigger tokens, and removes the backdoor from the compromised model. UNMASK exploits two fundamental properties of backdoor triggers, specificity and dominance, to assign a suspiciousness score to each input token. By leveraging two distinctive capabilities of MDLMs, parallel token prediction and token reconstruction

translated_title: 缓解掩码扩散语言模型中的后门
translated_abstract: 掩码扩散语言模型已成为自回归模型的一种有前景的替代方案，因为它们能够并行预测多个token，而不是按顺序生成token。然而，近期研究表明，掩码扩散语言模型容易受到后门攻击：当输入中包含攻击者选定的触发器时，被植入后门的模型会生成针对性的输出（例如恶意代码），而在其他情况下表现正常。尽管存在这一威胁，针对掩码扩散语言模型的后门防御在很大程度上仍未得到充分探索。我们提出了UNMASK，这是首个针对掩码扩散语言模型的防御框架，它能够检测包含触发器的输入、定位触发器token，并从受损模型中移除后门。UNMASK利用后门触发器的两个基本特性——特异性和主导性——为每个输入token分配可疑性评分。通过利用掩码扩散语言模型的两个独特能力——并行token预测和token重建……
tldr: 提出UNMASK，首个针对掩码扩散语言模型的后门防御框架，可检测含触发器的输入、定位触发token并从受损模型中移除后门。
en_tdlr: UNMASK, the first defense framework for masked diffusion language models, detects trigger-containing inputs, localizes trigger tokens, and removes backdoors from compromised models.
